title: Night shift shadow report — 2026-09-18
content:
Night shift shadow report — 18 Sep 2026

Summary:
- Shadow coverage 00:00–08:00 PT. Primary: Evan (shadow), Pager backup: Asha. No major customer-facing outage. Several degraded windows and an auto-scale misfire.
- Focus for the night: validate new autoscaler tweak (canary), confirm KV cache pressure alerts are stable, and triage a minor embedded-model flakiness from 03:10–03:24.

Incidents / Notable Events:
1) SRC-4127 — model-serving worker restart storm (03:09–03:40)
  - Trigger: sudden spike in ephemeral GPU OOMs from one dedicated pool after a low-memory quantized-model rollout at ~02:58 (canary).
  - Symptoms: ~12% increase in request latency P95 for dedicated-hosted routes and ~4% 5xx increase for ~30 minutes. No customer SLA break recorded, but elevated error budget consumption for dedicated customers.
  - Immediate mitigations taken:
    * rolled back canary variant to prior quantization profile at 03:12 (rollback happened automatically via rollout policy),
    * scaled up pool by +2 nodes as intermediate buffer at 03:15,
    * forced a GC and node-level diagnostic dump to GCS for offline analysis.
  - Timeline highlights:
    * 02:58 — canary roll started (model-q4_256_canary),
    * 03:05 — first OOM logged, automatic restart policy triggered,
    * 03:12 — rollback executed,
    * 03:20 — error rate trending down,
    * 03:40 — metrics returned to baseline.
  - Postmortem notes pending; preliminary hypothesis: quantized kernel memory estimator underestimates KV cache BLOBs when sequence length variance > baseline. Ticket created: SRE-4127.

2) KV Cache eviction jitter — intermittent (04:44–05:10)
  - Observed repeated cache-thrashing on a small subset of long-running requests for embeddings generation. Affected ~0.3% of total embedding calls.
  - Temporary workaround: enabled sticky-session affinity for those routes to reduce cache churn. Follow-up: run longer regression with synthetic long seqs.

SLO snapshot (current burn window):
- Text-generation availability (hosted api): 99.96% (target 99.95) — healthy, small buffer left.
- Dedicated tail latency (P95): 420ms (SLO 350ms) — currently 1.5x target at peak during the worker restart window, tracking.
- Error budget remaining (monthly): 68% (down 3% due to SRC-4127).

Alerts and signals triggered:
- alert-kv-cache-threshold (fired 04:42) — resolved after affinity change.
- autoscaler-latency-fallback (fired 03:10) — triggered by sudden drop in node health; autoscaler performed rollback.
- perf-regression-detect (noisy) — suppressed for the canary's rollout to avoid churn; flagged for tuning.

Handover / Day team asks (explicit):
- Engineering: validate quantized kernel memory-estimator across seq length distributions (see SRE-4127). Owner: Miguel. Due: 2026-09-20.
- Runbook: add a short checklist for recognizing the OOM/restart storm pattern and steps to increase pool capacity without impacting cost alerts. Owner: Evan/Asha. Due: 2026-09-22.
- Telemetry: add a short-term synthetic job to simulate high seq-variance traffic for dedicated pools (low-cost synthetic every 4h). Owner: Observability. Due: 2026-09-21.

Pending items I left for morning shift:
- Full diagnostic tarball uploaded to GCS (gs://redwood-debug/SRE-4127/2026-09-18/): confirm checksum and attach to ticket.
- Follow-up on GC logs from node gpool-ded-17 (OOM patterns around 03:05).
- Validate sticky-affinity experiment for embeddings under load; monitoring dashboard link in artifacts.

Notes to self / informal: 
- Observed some noisy logs from model-watcher that coincide with the rollout event; likely noisy, but might be hiding a scheduling edge-case.
- We suppressed perf-regression alerts for canary to avoid storming, but consider a middle-ground policy that rate-limits suppressions.

Action items (short):
- [ ] Miguel — run memory-estimator regression + reproduce with long-tail sequences. (SRE-4127)
- [ ] Asha — draft runbook fragment for restart-storm scenarios.
- [ ] Observability — schedule 4h synthetic job and add dashboard tile for seq-length distribution.
- [ ] Evan — attach debug tarball to ticket and start a lightweight RCA doc.

Meeting / sync requests:
- Quick sync with Runtime team 09/18 11:00 PT to review quantization knobs used in canary and confirm kernel selection logic (invitation sent to @runtime-eng).

Other housekeeping:
- Shift handover: left Vim bookmarks with log offsets in the diagnostic tarball for easier review.
- Leave a short note in #sre-night-ops with the TL;DR.

Appendix (quick links):
- Ticket: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/SRE-4127
- Debug tarball: gs://redwood-debug/SRE-4127/2026-09-18/
- Slack thread: https://slack.redwood.com/archives/C01BRIDGE/thread-09-18-2026
- Runbook PR (work in progress): https://github.com/redwood-inference/ops-runbooks/pull/128

End of night-shift shadow report.
